title: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
layout_note: Four lettered panels in dashed rounded frames: a wide panel A (corpus conversion: a real passage and its numbered propositions beside a Wikipedia -> Propositionizer -> FactoidWiki column), a tall panel B (query and corpus -> retriever -> stacks of passages, sentences, propositions), and two small stacked panels C (passage retrieval) and D (QA model) on the right.
grouping: Each panel is a dashed light-grey rounded frame with a black circled letter (A-D) at its top-left corner; inside A the source passage and its three propositions are joined to the database column by a callout-like outline; in B the three retrieval-unit stacks share one light-grey rounded tray.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with soft drop shadows; databases are cylinder stacks (blue for Wikipedia, crimson for FactoidWiki, grey for the generic corpus); retrieval units are small grey cards with grey text bars, stacked with offsets; the query is a yellow card with brown text bars and a question mark; the answer a green card with green bars and a tick; module boxes (Propositionizer, Retriever) are white with thick grey outlines.
proposed_highlight: The new corpus is named in a saturated colour of its own: FactoidWiki is a crimson database whose pink tint fills each numbered proposition box in panel A, against the blue tint of the Wikipedia source passage; panel A is the widest panel.
lesson: Show a corpus transformation by setting one real source passage, tinted like its source database, above the units it is split into, tinted like the output database, beside a short database -> module -> database column.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first-page header ('EMNLP 2024 Main Conference'). id uses the title's name 'Dense X Retrieval'. 'other' element: abstract document cards (grey text bars) standing in for retrieval units, queries and answers. In panel A the source passage carries small '//' marks where it is split.

arrangement.units: four dashed rounded frames lettered A-D: A (corpus construction) spans the left ~45 %, B (retrieval) a tall middle panel, C (passage retrieval) and D (QA model) stacked on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted Wikipedia paragraph in a blue-tinted box, split below into three numbered pink proposition boxes; the query as an abstract yellow card
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the evaluation tasks are panels C and D
arrangement.shared: the retrieval-unit card glyph is reused in B and C (D switches to rows of grey squares); the yellow query card appears in B and D

taxonomy.task: dense retrieval and open-domain QA over a corpus indexed at passage, sentence or proposition granularity

insights.structure: A wide left panel teaches the corpus conversion with a real example; a middle panel shows retrieval returning three granularities; two small right panels name the downstream evaluations.
insights.data: The source paragraph and its three propositions are quoted verbatim in tinted boxes, while retrieval units elsewhere are abstract grey cards whose stacks shrink from passages to propositions.
insights.emphasis: The new corpus FactoidWiki and its propositions share one crimson/pink family that appears nowhere else, and panel A takes the most area.
insights.flow: Short straight grey arrows run top to bottom inside each panel (Wikipedia -> Propositionizer -> FactoidWiki; query and corpus -> Retriever -> units); panels are read A to D left to right without arrows between them.
insights.avoid: Panel C's glyph (a unit stack, a curved arrow, unit cards dropped into blue passage boxes, two outlined) is not decodable without the text, and D redraws units as square rows; keep one glyph per noun and do not reduce an evaluation setting to an unlabelled icon arrangement.

core.what: Wikipedia -> Propositionizer -> FactoidWiki as a short vertical column, with one real passage beside it split into its numbered propositions, so the corpus conversion is seen on its data

relations.form: a vertical column in panel A: blue Wikipedia cylinder, white Propositionizer box, crimson FactoidWiki cylinder, joined by short down arrows
the conversion is drawn on one quoted paragraph: the blue passage box above, a down arrow, three pink numbered proposition boxes below, '//' marks at the split points
in panel B three card stacks of shrinking size (Passages, Sentences, Propositions) sit side by side in one grey tray under the retriever
panel B: query card and grey corpus cylinder side by side at the top, arrows converging down into one Retriever box, then down to the unit tray
panel D: the query card and two rows of retrieval units sit together inside one thick-outlined QA Model frame, with one arrow out to a green Answer card

channels.colour: colour = data kind: blue = Wikipedia passages (the source passage box, the Wikipedia cylinder, and the passage boxes in panel C), crimson/pink = FactoidWiki propositions, yellow = query, green = answer, grey = generic units and corpus
channels.shape: cylinders = corpora, white thick-outlined rounded boxes = modules, small grey cards with bars = retrieval units, tinted text boxes = quoted data
channels.line: one style: short grey straight arrows for data flow; one curved black arrow in panel C
channels.frame: dashed rounded frame = one panel with one job; a thick solid frame in D = the QA model containing its inputs

quality.strengths: Panel A draws the contribution on real data: the same passage is shown before and after propositionizing, and its tints match the two databases, so the conversion reads without labels. The three granularities are compared as side-by-side stacks of shrinking size in one tray. Panel A, the novelty, is the widest; all arrows are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: Panels C and D are abstract: C places unit cards into blue passage boxes, two of them outlined, with a curved arrow, and what this measures needs the caption; D draws the retrieval units as rows of grey squares, a different glyph from the cards in B and C. Panel B's proposition stack is grey, not the FactoidWiki pink, so the tie from A to B is carried by labels only.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
